COMES NOW Jason Price, Party No. 200 as identified in Attachment B, and Jessica Price to the
Procedural Order, appearing Pro Se, and respectfully file this Motion to Enter Direct Testimony
and Exhibits, and in support thereof would show the following:

1. On May 13, 2026, Jason Price and Jessica Price timely filed their Direct Testimony and
Exhibits with the Public Utility Commission of Texas. Docket filing number 4477.

2. Shortly after filing their Direct Testimony with the Public Utility Commission of Texas,
Jason Price and Jessica Price departed the United States for previously planned
international travel. Upon their return to the United States, they learned for the first
time that filing procedures required testimony and exhibits to also be uploaded
through the Egnyte and Kiteworks systems. By the time they became aware of this
additional requirement, the filing deadline had already passed. Jason Price and
Jessica Price respectfully submit that the failure to upload the testimony and
exhibits through those systems was inadvertent and not intended to delay or
prejudice any party in this proceeding.

3. Upon becoming aware of the additional filing requirements, Jason Price and Jessica Price
promptly took steps to provide the testimony and exhibits to all required parties.

4. Jason Price and Jessica Price respectfully request that the attached testimony and exhibit

be accepted into the record and considered by the State Office of Administrative

Hearings and all parties in this proceeding.

Jason Price and Jessica Price are appearing Pro Se in this matter.

Jason Price and Jessica Price do not intend to call any witnesses other than themselves.

Jason Price and Jessica Price do not request cross-examination.

The attached Direct Testimony is offered as Exhibit 1. The attached Photographic

Exhibits Supporting the Direct Testimony of Jason Price and Jessica Price are offered

as Exhibit 2.

PERSONAL INFORMATION:

Q. Please state your name and address.

A. Our names are Jason and Jessica Price.
Our address is 7972 Dice Grove Rd., Belton, TX 76513

Q. Have you filed a Motion to Intervene in this proceeding?

A. Yes.

Q. What link and tracts are you testifying in representation of today?
A. Track 3027 and Link E11

Q. Are you testifying on behalf of anyone, or just yourself?

A. Ourselves

Q. How is the property affected by the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV

transmission line project proposed by Oncor and LCRA TSC?

A. Response to Question: “How is the property affected by the Bell County East to Big Hill
765kV transmission line project proposed by Oncor and LCRA TSC?”

Jason Price and I are residents, heirs, and future stewards of a generational family ranch located
in Bell County, Texas. While we currently own our residence located on the ranch property, our
family ranch and the surrounding family land will be directly and severely impacted by the
proposed Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV transmission line project, specifically proposed
Link E11 and Link Cl.

The ranch was purchased in 1989 by Dr. Larry Price, Jason’s father, and it has remained in our
family ever since. This ranch is not simply an investment property. It is our forever home, where
we are raising our children and where our family intends to remain for generations to come.
Jason Price has lived on this ranch since he was a young child and is an heir to the ranch
property. Our children have been raised here since they were babies, and our oldest child plans to

build a home on the ranch within the next few years. This property is intended to be passed down
through future generations of our family.

The proposed Link E11 would place transmission towers and lines directly on our ranch and
would run parallel to our driveway. Proposed Link C1 would run parallel along the side of our
ranch directly across the street from our property. At one point, there would be less than 50 feet
between the two proposed links near the entrance gate to our home. That entrance gate is
approximately 700 feet from our residence, meaning our family would essentially be surrounded
by major transmission infrastructure.

Additionally, there is already an existing large transmission line, known as the Schwertner Line,
located along one side of the ranch. Proposed Link C1 would run parallel to this existing line,
further increasing the concentration of transmission infrastructure surrounding our home, ranch
operations, livestock, wildlife habitat, and future family development areas.

The proposed towers associated with Link E11 would be located within approximately 250 feet
of our front door. Additionally, our ranch contains four other residences. One residence is
located approximately 275 feet from a proposed tower location and was not marked on the
project maps as being within 500 feet of the transmission line. The remaining homes on the
ranch would also have direct views of the towers and lines, permanently impacting the
residential nature of the property and the quality of life for those living there.

Our ranch spans approximately 500 acres and is actively used for ranching, farming, hunting,
residential purposes, and several business operations. We raise registered cattle, grow hay,
harvest pecans, breed and raise racehorses, and maintain barns, equipment facilities, and a horse
arena. The ranch is also used as a venue for weddings, family gatherings, and photography
sessions, including professional family and engagement photos. The natural beauty, open
landscapes, mature oak trees, creeks, and scenic views are a major reason people choose our
property for these events and photography opportunities. The placement of massive transmission
towers and high-voltage lines throughout the ranch would permanently destroy the visual appeal
and peaceful atmosphere that make these activities possible.

The proposed line would place towers and infrastructure less than 300 feet from our barns and
horse arena. The project would also take several acres of land out of productive use and
permanently impact the only field on the ranch currently suitable for future residential
development for our children and family members.

The proposed transmission links would cross streams, waterways, roadways, and
environmentally sensitive areas throughout the ranch. Much of the ranch lies within a flood plain
and is also located on a fault line, creating additional concerns regarding erosion, soil stability,
drainage, and long-term infrastructure impacts. Due to this fault line, our ranch also contains a
large area with an abundance of Exogyra fossils and quartz deposits, which are unique natural
and geological featurcs of the property. These areas contribute to the environmental and
historical significance of the ranch and would be at risk from construction disturbance,
excavation, and long-term infrastructure impacts.

The ranch contains two natural springs, one of which would be located directly beneath the
proposed transmission lines. Moon Branch Creek also runs beneath the proposed line route and
contains a natural spring that feeds into Salado Creek, which then flows into the Lampasas River
watershed and beyond. These waterways and springs are vital natural resources that support
wildlife, livestock, water flow, and the environmental health of the surrounding area. The project
threatens drainage patterns, water resources, erosion control, and the long-term environmental
stability of the property. An active water well located approximately 300 feet from the proposed
line was also not identified on the project maps.

Additionally, a family cemetery located on the ranch was not marked on the maps and would be
within view of the proposed E11 line. This cemetery is deeply important to our family and
represents generations of family history tied to this land.

The construction and long-term operation of this project would create significant disruption to
agricultural operations, including impacts to livestock movement, grazing patterns, crop
production, hay production, fencing, roadway access, and general ranch operations. Construction
activities would heavily damage pastures and fields, and recovery could take years. Large
portions of mature oak trees would also be removed for tower placement and right-of-way
clearing, permanently altering the landscape and destroying trees that have existed on this
property for generations.

The project would also negatively affect wildlife and natural habitats on the ranch. Our property
supports deer populations, fish within the streams and ponds, and a growing turkey population
that has taken years to reestablish in the area. Over the years, rare bird species have also been
observed on the ranch. The clearing of trees, placement of massive towers, increased noise, and
ongoing disturbance associated with the transmission line would permanently impact wildlife
patterns and habitat.

We also have serious concerns regarding constant EMF exposure and noise associated with the
proposed transmission lines and towers. The audible humming and industrial presence of the
infrastructure would significantly interfere with the peaceful residential and rural nature of our
home and ranch.

The economic impact to our family would be devastating. Our residence sits on approximately
two acres and is currently valued at approximately $1.1 million. The overall ranch property
consists of approximately 500 acres with an estimated value of at least $25 million. The
placement of high-voltage transmission lines and towers throughout the property would
substantially devalue both the residential and agricultural portions of the ranch. The project
would also limit future residential expansion plans, commercial growth opportunities, wedding
and photography use of the property, and retirement plans for our family.

We were also not properly notified regarding impacts to additional portions of our ranch
identified as Tracts 3025 and 3026. We are listed on Tract 3027, but significant surrounding
portions of our ranch are included within Tracts 3025 and 3026. The lack of proper notification

Our future plans for this ranch include continuing our ranching and farming operations,
expanding our businesses, building additional homes for family members, and ultimately retiring
here. The proposed transmission project threatens every one of those plans and fundamentally
changes the future of our property, our family legacy, and the long-term future of this land.

For these reasons, we strongly oppose the proposed Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV
transmission line links affecting our property and respectfully request that the proposed links be
denied or relocated away from our home, ranch, water resources, businesses, natural springs,
creeks, geological features, family cemetery, and family lands.

Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?

A. ‘he purpose of my testimony is to explain how the proposed Bell County East to Big Hill
765kV transmission line project will directly and negatively impact Jason and me, our home,
generational family ranch, businesses, livestock operations, water resources, wildlife, property
values, and our family’s future plans for the land. My testimony is also intended to demonstrate
why the proposed links should be denied or relocated away from our property and surrounding

family lands.

Q. What routes do you oppose?

A. Jason and | oppose all proposed routes that include Link E11 and Link C1 associated

with the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV transmission line project.

Q. What routes do you support?

A. None

Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?
A. No

PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND HISTORY

Q. Can you please describe the affected property, including the legal description

from the County CAD?

A. The affected property is a generational family ranch located in Bell County, Texas,
consisting of approximately 500 acres used for residential, ranching, farming, hunting,
and business purposes. The affected areas include Tracts 3025, 3026, and 3027 as
identified in the proposed Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV transmission line project.
The legal description on Bell County Appraisal District for Tract 3025 & 3026 are
Residential/Farm/Ranch, Tract 3027 is just Residential.

Q. Can you please explain your history and familiarity with the affected property,

including its current usage?
A. The line will go along our driveway

Q. Can you please include any pictures with dates that depict the property and

how it is used?

A. Yes

Q. Have the pictures been altered?

A. No

Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?
A. Yes

Q. How would the proposed transmission line interfere with your current land

use?

A. The proposed transmission line would significantly interfere with the family’s current use of
the property for ranching, farming, residential living, hunting, livestock operations, hay
production, and business purposes. The proposed links would place large transmission towers
and high-voltage lines near our home, other residences on the ranch, barns, horse arena,
roadways, streams, ponds, and grazing areas.

Construction and long-term maintenance of the transmission line would disrupt livestock
movement, damage pastures and hay fields, remove mature oak trees, impact water resources and
drainage patterns, and reduce the usability of several acres of the ranch. The proposed links
would also interfere with future plans for additional family homes, business expansion, and
continued agricultural use of the property. In addition, the constant visual impact, noise, and
EMF concerns associated with the transmission line would permanently affect the peaceful
residential and rural nature of our home and family ranch.

Q. Are there any specific structures or features that would be within 500 feet of

any of the proposed routes?

A. Yes. Structures and features within 500 feet of the proposed links include Jason’s and my
home, which would be approximately 250 feet from the proposed towers associated with Link
E11. Other structures located along E11 are another residence on the ranch located
approximately 275 feet (not marked on the map), barns, a horse arena valued just under $1
million, ranch roadways, streams, ponds, and an active water well located approximately 300
feet from the proposed line(not marked on the map).

Q. In your opinion, how will this project affect the value of your land?

A. In my opinion, the proposed transmission project would substantially decrease the value of
Jason’s and my property and the surrounding family ranch land. Our home alone is currently
valued at approximately $1.1 million, and the overall ranch property is estimated to be worth at
least $25 million. Having large 765kV transmission towers and high-voltage power lines located
within close proximity to our home, other residences, barns, horse arena, waterways, and future
homesites would make the property significantly less desirable and negatively impact both
residential and agricultural value.

The proposed links would also reduce the usable acreage of the ranch, interfere with future
development plans for family homes and business expansion, and permanently alter the
appearance and character of the property. In my opinion, the visual impact, noise, EMF
concerns, loss of trees, and industrialization of the land could reduce portions of the property
value by as much as 45%.

ENVIRONMENTAL AND AESTHETIC IMPACTS (16 TAC § 25.101)

Q. What are your concerns regarding the local environment and wildlife?

A. Jason and I are very concerned about the long-term impact the proposed transmission line
would have on the local environment and wildlife habitat on and around our ranch. The proposed
links would require the removal of mature oak trees and would cross streams, creeks, ponds, and
areas near Salado Creek, which could negatively affect water quality, drainage, erosion control,
and the overall health of the land.

Our ranch supports a wide variety of wildlife, including deer, fish, and a growing turkey
population that has taken years to reestablish in the area. Rare bird species have also been
spotted on the property over the years. The clearing of land, construction activity, tower
placement, increased human activity, and long-term noise from the transmission lines could
permanently disrupt wildlife patterns, nesting areas, migration paths, and natural habitats.

In addition, we are concerned about the overall environmental impact of placing massive
transmission infrastructure throughout productive agricultural land and sensitive natural areas
that our family has worked hard to preserve for future generations.

Q. How will the line affect the "aesthetic values" (the look and feel) of your area?

A. The proposed transmission line would permanently and drastically change the aesthetic values
of Jason’s and my property and surrounding community. Our area is currently made up of open
fields, mature trees, creeks, ranchland, and natural views with very little visible development.
From our home, we cannot even see another house, only fields, wildlife, and trees.

The proposed project would replace those natural rural views with massive 765kV transmission
towers and high-voltage power lines, including towers located directly in front of our home.

Instead of looking out at peaceful ranchland, our family and community would be forced to look
at large industrial infrastructure dominating the landscape.

In my opinion, the project would destroy the rural beauty, peaceful atmosphere, and scenic
character that make this area special and that families like ours have worked hard to preserve for
generations.

LOCAL NEED AND COST (PURA § 37.056)

Q. Do you believe this project provides a direct benefit to your local electric

service?

A. No. In my opinion, this project does not provide a direct benefit to Jason’s and my local
clectric service that would outweigh the permanent impacts and damage it would cause to our
home, family ranch, property values, businesses, natural resources, and rural community.

Q. Do you believe this project will decrease your electric cost?

A. No. I do not believe this project will decrease Jason’s and my electric costs. In my opinion,
projects of this size could potentially lead to increased electrical costs or fees for customers in
order to cover the cost of construction and long-term maintenance of the transmission line
project.

RECREATION AND COMMUNITY VALUES

Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?

A. The proposed transmission line would drastically affect Jason’s and my enjoyment of our
property and home. One of the reasons we chose to build and raise our family here is because of
the peace, privacy, and natural beauty of the ranch. From our home, we currently cannot even see
another house — all we see are open fields, mature oak trees, pastures, and wildlife. The
proposed project would permanently change that by placing massive 765kV transmission towers
and high-voltage power lines directly in front of our home and throughout the ranch.

Instead of enjoying the natural landscape and peaceful rural setting, we would be forced to look
at large industrial towers, hear constant noise from the lines, and live with ongoing concerns
about EMF exposure and safety. The transmission infrastructure would completely alter the
character of our home, reduce our privacy, and destroy the quiet enjoyment of the property that
our family has valued for generations.

Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use

on your land?

A. Yes. The proposed transmission line would negatively affect several planned future uses for
Jason’s and my land. Our family intends to continue using the ranch for ranching, farming,
hunting, livestock operations, hay production, residential living, and business purposes. We also
plan to retire on this property and continue passing the ranch down through future generations.

In addition, our oldest child plans to build a home on the ranch within the next few years, and we
had planned to use the only suitable field on the property for future family homesites. The
proposed links and tower locations would directly impact that area and significantly limit future
residential development opportunities for our family.

The project would also interfere with plans to expand our businesses and continue improving the
ranch for future generations. The placement of large transmission towers, loss of usable acreage,
damage to the natural landscape, and long-term impacts to property value would permanently
affect the future use and development of our land.

Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your

area?

A. The proposed transmission line would significantly damage the rural community values that
Jason and I, along with many others in our area, have worked hard to preserve. Our community
values open land, agriculture, ranching, wildlife, privacy, peace, and respect for generational
family properties. This area has remained rural because families here have chosen to protect and
care for the land rather than overdevelop it.

Placing massive 765kV transmission towers and high-voltage power lines throughout our
community would permanently change the character of the area from a peaceful rural landscape
to an industrial corridor. The project would negatively impact family ranches, homes,
agriculture, natural beauty, wildlife habitat, and the quiet way of life that draws families to this
area.

In my opinion, this project goes against the values of rural Texas communities and threatens the
long-term future of the land, families, and agricultural heritage that make this area special.

Direct Testimony of Jason and Jessica Price
PUC Docket No. 59475

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349

CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

Q. What is your recommendation to the Commission?

A. My recommendation to the Commission is to deny the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV
transmission line project in its entirety. In my opinion, the project would cause unnecessary and
permanent harm to family homes, generational ranches, agricultural operations, wildlife habitat,
water resources, and rural communities throughout Bell County and the surrounding areas.

The proposed project places an unfair burden on landowners and families who have spent
generations building and preserving their land and way of life. I believe the long-term negative

impacts to private property rights, property values, natural resources, and the rural character of
our community far outweigh any claimed benefit of the project.

I respectfully ask the Commission to protect Texas landowners, families, and future generations
by stopping this project.

Q. Does this conclude your testimony?

A. Yes.

The proposed Link E11 would place transmission towers and lines directly on our ranch and
would run parallel to our driveway. Proposed Link C1 would run parallel along the side of our

approximately 700 feet from our residence, meaning our family would essentially be surrounded
by major transmission infrastructure.

Additionally, there is already an existing large transmission line, known as the Schwertner Line,
located along one side of the ranch. Proposed Link C1 would run parallel to this existing line,
further increasing the concentration of transmission infrastructure surrounding our home, ranch

The proposed towers associated with Link E11 would be located within approximately 250 feet

Our ranch spans approximately 500 acres and is actively used for ranching, farming, hunting,

historical significance of the ranch and would be at risk from construction disturbance,
excavation, and long-term infrastructure impacts.

ENVIRONMENTAL AND AESTHETIC IMPACTS (16 TAC § 25.101)

Q. What are your concerns regarding the local environment and wildlife?

A. Jason and I are very concerned about the long-term impact the proposed transmission line
would have on the local environment and wildlife habitat on and around our ranch. The proposed
links would require the removal of mature oak trees and would cross streams, creeks, ponds, and
areas near Salado Creek, which could negatively affect water quality, drainage, erosion control,
and the overall health of the land.

Our ranch supports a wide variety of wildlife, including deer, fish, and a growing turkey
population that has taken years to reestablish in the area. Rare bird species have also been
spotted on the property over the years. The clearing of land, construction activity, tower
placement, increased human activity, and long-term noise from the transmission lines could
permanently disrupt wildlife patterns, nesting areas, migration paths, and natural habitats.

In addition, we are concerned about the overall environmental impact of placing massive
transmission infrastructure throughout productive agricultural land and sensitive natural areas
that our family has worked hard to preserve for future generations.

Q. How will the line affect the "aesthetic values" (the look and feel) of your area?

A. The proposed transmission line would permanently and drastically change the aesthetic values
of Jason’s and my property and surrounding community. Our area is currently made up of open
fields, mature trees, creeks, ranchland, and natural views with very little visible development.
From our home, we cannot even see another house, only fields, wildlife, and trees.

The proposed project would replace those natural rural views with massive 765kV transmission
towers and high-voltage power lines, including towers located directly in front of our home.
Instead of looking out at peaceful ranchland, our family and community would be forced to look
at large industrial infrastructure dominating the landscape.

In my opinion, the project would destroy the rural beauty, peaceful atmosphere, and scenic
character that make this area special and that families like ours have worked hard to preserve for
generations.
